column1: Construction contractors|contract milestones, retainage, and equipment commitments|job-cost reports; open contracts; equipment schedules|Compare the timing of customer collections with payroll and project spending before committing to a new job.|Who will connect job-level reporting with the owner’s planning calendar?

Residential home builders|land, work in progress, and closings|project budgets; lot inventory; closing schedules|Separate development cash needs from the owner’s available cash when reviewing the next build.|How will the engagement distinguish project entities and unsold inventory?

Commercial builders|long projects, subcontractor commitments, and multiple project entities|contract summaries; retainage schedules; subcontractor ledger|Ask the candidate to explain how it gathers information across project managers and the accounting team.|Who reviews the records when a contract’s scope or expected completion changes?

Roofing companies|seasonal crews, materials, and storm-related demand|crew payroll; materials purchases; job margins|Use a representative busy-season month to show the relationship between volume, cash, and staffing.|How will seasonal operating changes be reflected in the review?

HVAC companies|service agreements, installations, and technician capacity|maintenance contracts; installation margins; vehicle schedules|Separate recurring maintenance work from larger installations when explaining the operating business.|Which reports are needed to understand the service and installation sides together?

Plumbing businesses|dispatch work, projects, and owner field responsibilities|dispatch reports; project invoices; payroll roles|Describe the owner’s fieldwork and management responsibilities alongside company finances.|How do you distinguish owner duties from the work performed by employees?

Electrical contractors|project billing, licensing jurisdictions, and equipment|project ledger; jurisdiction list; equipment records|Identify where employees perform work and where project records are maintained.|Who coordinates the project location information with the filing team?

Landscaping companies|seasonal revenue, crews, and equipment replacement|seasonal budgets; crew costs; asset list|Bring a full operating cycle so a busy quarter does not become the only basis for the discussion.|How will off-season cash needs enter the planning analysis?

Restoration businesses|insurance-related collections and subcontracted projects|claims receivables; job-cost reports; vendor contracts|Distinguish an approved invoice from cash actually available to the business.|Who will reconcile project status with customer and insurer collections?

Property management firms|management fees, owner accounts, and affiliated properties|management agreements; entity map; fee reports|Keep client funds, operating revenue, and personally held property interests distinct.|How will related entities and managed client accounts be separated in the work?

Commercial landlords|leases, financing, and property entities|rent rolls; loan summaries; property schedules|Organize the properties by entity and upcoming lease or financing event.|Who will coordinate property records with the professional preparing each return?

Residential rental owners|property-level records and household planning|property ledger; ownership map; depreciation schedules|Use property-by-property records to explain a portfolio rather than one combined income figure.|Which property documents will be reviewed before a study or other project is proposed?

Short-term rental operators|booking channels, management responsibilities, and property costs|booking exports; operating agreements; activity records|Describe how each rental is operated and who performs the work, using contemporaneous records.|How will the proposed review distinguish each property’s operating facts?

Real estate developers|land, development entities, and project financing|capital stack; entity agreements; project timeline|Identify the next binding commitment and the professionals already involved in the development.|Who models the alternatives when the financing or development timeline changes?

Real estate brokerages|commission collections, teams, and owner production|commission statements; team contracts; owner role summary|Separate the owner’s selling activity from brokerage management when describing the business.|How will agent and team arrangements be reflected in the engagement?

Dental practices|clinical work, practice ownership, and equipment|practice financials; owner payroll; equipment proposals|Bring the practice’s operating needs and the owner’s household priorities into the same brief.|Who coordinates with the practice bookkeeper and benefits administrator?

Medical practices|multiple providers, collection timing, and ownership agreements|collection reports; partner agreements; payroll roster|Identify which decisions belong to the practice and which belong to individual owners.|How will partner-specific questions be separated from the practice-wide scope?

Veterinary practices|clinical services, inventory, and facility commitments|service mix; inventory reports; lease documents|Explain the relationship between service revenue, pharmacy inventory, and facility spending.|Which specialist or administrator relationships will the advisor need to coordinate?

Physical therapy practices|provider scheduling, reimbursement, and expansion|payer mix; payroll; location budgets|Describe how a new clinician or location changes costs before collections arrive.|How will location-level reporting support the proposed analysis?

Mental health practices|clinician arrangements, collections, and owner workload|clinician agreements; collection reports; owner duties|Clarify the relationship between clinicians, the practice, and the owner’s professional work.|Which facts about clinician arrangements need review by other professionals?

Optometry practices|clinical services, retail inventory, and equipment|retail margins; service revenue; equipment list|Separate retail and clinical economics so the candidate understands both operating activities.|How will the engagement capture the practice’s service and retail components?

Law firms|partner compensation, client collections, and operating accounts|partnership agreements; compensation schedule; receivables|Keep client account responsibilities distinct from firm operating cash and owner distributions.|How are partner-level questions and firm-level deliverables assigned?

Consulting firms|project fees, utilization, and subcontracted delivery|project profitability; contracts; contractor ledger|Show the candidate how fees are earned and how the delivery team is paid.|Which reports will be used to distinguish growth from cash available to owners?

Accounting firms|partner responsibilities, recurring work, and acquired clients|partner agreements; service mix; client acquisition terms|Describe the advisory gap and independence requirements before requesting outside assistance.|How will the proposed engagement interact with the firm’s existing professional obligations?

Architecture firms|project phases, retainers, and partner roles|project backlog; phase budgets; partner duties|Identify which projects are in design, delivery, or collection when discussing the year ahead.|How will work in progress and partner responsibilities inform the planning brief?

Engineering consultancies|technical projects, staffing, and contract milestones|project margins; staffing plan; customer contracts|Distinguish signed backlog from expected revenue and collected cash.|Who will update the analysis when staffing or project timing changes?

Marketing agencies|retainers, campaign projects, and contractor teams|client contracts; delivery margins; contractor costs|Separate recurring account work from project launches and media pass-through spending.|How will the scope distinguish agency revenue from customer-funded spending?

Advertising agencies|campaign budgets, production vendors, and client billing|campaign ledger; vendor terms; billing schedules|Explain the timing between supplier commitments and customer payment.|Who reconciles campaign economics with the company’s operating reports?

Creative studios|project deposits, production costs, and intellectual property|project contracts; production budgets; rights agreements|Bring the contracts that explain what the studio delivers and retains after a project.|Which contract questions require legal input alongside the financial review?

Software companies|subscriptions, development spending, and ownership changes|subscription reports; development budgets; capitalization table|Identify product investment and ownership decisions separately from recurring operating revenue.|Who coordinates the financial analysis with counsel and the company’s finance team?

SaaS businesses|renewals, billing terms, and customer acquisition spending|recurring revenue reports; billing schedules; customer acquisition budget|Distinguish bookings, recognized revenue, and collections when preparing the business summary.|Which definitions of growth and cash will the advisor use in the analysis?

AI startups|product investment, funding, and commercial contracts|funding documents; product budget; customer agreements|Explain the actual products, customers, and financing arrangements rather than relying on the startup label.|Which financing and intellectual-property questions need a specialist review?

IT service providers|managed contracts, hardware resale, and technician teams|service agreements; hardware margins; payroll|Separate recurring managed services from equipment resale and project work.|How will the proposed review capture the different revenue streams?

Cybersecurity firms|professional engagements, subscriptions, and staffing|engagement contracts; subscription agreements; staffing plan|Identify which commitments involve ongoing services and which involve discrete projects.|Who will coordinate timing changes across client contracts and staffing?

Ecommerce brands|inventory, sales channels, and fulfillment|channel reports; inventory valuation records; fulfillment agreements|Show the movement from gross platform sales to collected cash after returns and fees.|How will channel and marketplace information be gathered and reconciled?

Online retailers|purchasing cycles, returns, and marketplace fees|supplier terms; returns reports; platform statements|Keep product purchasing commitments visible alongside sales forecasts.|Which reports are needed to evaluate cash needs across the sales channels?

Wholesale distributors|inventory financing, customer credit, and supplier terms|inventory aging; receivables; credit agreements|Compare supplier payment dates with expected customer collections.|Who reviews the assumptions behind purchasing and customer credit decisions?

Manufacturers|production costs, inventory, and capital investment|production reports; bill of materials; capital budget|Explain the link between production capacity, inventory, and the next investment.|Which operating reports will be reconciled to the financial records?

Machine shops|custom jobs, equipment capacity, and skilled labor|job margins; machine schedules; equipment proposals|Bring a representative job and the assumptions behind the next equipment purchase.|Who connects capacity planning with the proposed financial review?

Food manufacturers|production batches, inventory, and distribution|batch costs; inventory records; distributor terms|Separate manufacturing costs from channel and distribution costs.|How will the engagement handle product and channel-level information?

Consumer product brands|product launches, wholesale channels, and inventory|launch budgets; channel margins; inventory schedules|Identify commitments made before a product launch generates collections.|Which launch assumptions will be documented and revisited?

Restaurants|location economics, labor, and food costs|location profit reports; payroll; lease terms|Show the candidate an ordinary operating period and a peak period for each location.|Who will separate owner-level questions from location operating needs?

Restaurant groups|multiple locations, shared services, and ownership|entity map; intercompany charges; location budgets|Map which entity owns each location and which expenses are shared.|How will shared costs and owner arrangements be documented for review?

Catering businesses|event deposits, seasonal demand, and staffing|event contracts; deposit schedule; temporary staffing costs|Bring the timing of deposits and event expenses into the planning discussion.|How are cancelled events or changing bookings reflected in the records?

Hotels|room revenue, property costs, and management arrangements|occupancy reports; property schedule; management contracts|Separate the operating hotel from the ownership and financing of its real estate.|Who coordinates operating and property-level review across the entities?

Franchise operators|unit economics, royalties, and expansion agreements|franchise agreements; unit reports; expansion budget|Identify which decisions are controlled by the franchise agreement and which remain with the owner.|Which agreement terms should be reviewed with counsel before modeling a change?

Trucking companies|fleet commitments, driver arrangements, and routes|fleet schedule; driver agreements; route margins|Describe the fleet ownership and payment arrangements as well as route economics.|Who gathers the jurisdiction and equipment records required for the scope?

Logistics providers|customer contracts, subcontractors, and facility commitments|customer terms; subcontractor ledger; facility leases|Explain which services are performed directly and which are provided through partners.|How will the engagement map the different operating responsibilities?

Warehousing businesses|facility leases, labor, and customer inventory|facility costs; service contracts; staffing reports|Keep customer-owned inventory separate from the operator’s own assets and financial records.|Who confirms the ownership and accounting treatment of stored goods?

Staffing agencies|payroll timing, customer credit, and placements|payroll schedule; receivables; placement agreements|Make the gap between paying workers and collecting from customers visible.|Which reports will support the review of working capital and growth plans?

Recruiting firms|placement fees, guarantees, and contractor costs|placement contracts; fee schedules; contractor ledger|Explain fee triggers and guarantee periods instead of supplying only annual revenue.|How will changing placement timing affect the assumptions reviewed?

Cleaning companies|recurring contracts, crews, and supplies|customer agreements; crew costs; vehicle records|Separate contract work from one-time projects when preparing the operating summary.|Who coordinates crew and location information with the company’s records?

Security companies|staffing contracts, licensing areas, and insurance costs|service contracts; staffing roster; jurisdiction list|Describe where the work is performed and which entity carries each contract.|Which licensing and employment questions should be assigned to other professionals?

Auto repair shops|labor, parts inventory, and shop equipment|repair-order reports; parts inventory; equipment schedules|Separate labor and parts margins when explaining the shop’s economics.|Which reports will the advisor need from the shop management system?

Auto dealerships|vehicle inventory, floorplan financing, and related entities|inventory schedules; financing terms; entity map|Identify the relationships between the dealership, real estate, and financing arrangements.|How will the proposed work coordinate the distinct entities and specialists?

Fitness studios|memberships, instructor arrangements, and locations|membership reports; instructor agreements; location budgets|Distinguish recurring memberships from classes, personal training, and retail sales.|How will the engagement capture each service and location’s operating facts?

Salons and spas|service teams, product sales, and facility commitments|service revenue; worker agreements; product inventory|Explain the business’s team arrangements and separate service from retail activity.|Which questions about worker arrangements need coordinated legal review?

Childcare businesses|enrollment, staffing requirements, and facility costs|enrollment schedules; payroll roster; lease terms|Describe capacity, staffing, and facility commitments using current operating records.|How will the review account for the business’s operating constraints?

Agricultural businesses|production cycles, land, and equipment|production records; land agreements; equipment schedule|Use a full production cycle to explain cash needs and commitments.|Who will distinguish operating, land, and household records in the engagement?

Renewable energy contractors|project commitments, equipment, and specialist coordination|project contracts; installation budgets; equipment records|Identify the parties making commitments and the project milestones requiring review.|Which project-specific tax or legal questions require a specialist engagement?
